items.summary: Recommendation: maintain financial containment and reject all three new preview change requests this cycle. Revenue evidence covers only 2026-09-21: 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission; the aggregate amount is not site-attributable. AI usage covers 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-28: 4,926 calls, 228 errors, and $901.90 recorded cost. Contribution margin, ROI, payback, cost-to-learn, infrastructure spend, and budget exposure are not calculable because revenue and cost periods do not align, infrastructure/domain/labor/marketing/experiment costs are incomplete, monthly budget ceilings are blank, and no learning-outcome threshold exists. The 36 improvements awaiting measurement, 9 failed requests, and 3 proven outcomes are operational status, not financial performance. Retain existing reconciliation only; do not dispatch, spend, deploy, requeue, expand monetization, or make revenue claims.

Retain and continue the existing affiliate-attribution reconciliation work only. Compare existing registry, rendered affiliate URLs, provider tracking rows, and matching-period cost records. Preserve the $4.92 aggregate provider row as unattributed; do not convert clicks, orders, shipped items, sessions, conversions, AI calls, or output counts into revenue, margin, ROI, payback, or causal-lift claims.

Do not retain the proposed drivegm.net, failbunny.com, or mynewgm.com change requests for execution. Preserve them as deferred backlog only until existing ownership, failure-repair, release, security, attribution, rollback, and measurement gates clear. Their preview validation metrics may be recorded as operational evidence, but no financial return or learning value should be claimed without a defined outcome and cost ceiling.

Continue existing period-aligned reconciliation and preserve unknowns. Minimum finance evidence remains: matching-period attributable revenue, complete recorded cost categories including AI and infrastructure, approved budget ceilings, and an explicit learning outcome and maximum cost-to-learn. Do not create duplicate telemetry or financial work.
